text:
sara: FYI — ACME is reporting repeated 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. They say streaming cuts out mid-response and retries spike. sample request ids: r-9a1c, r-9a1d, r-9a1e. customers on eu-west.
ops-bot: Alert: hosted-upstream-runner-crash (5 events in 12m) — https://sentry.company/issue/98765 : signal=11 / cuda error OOM logged
 tom: which pool & model? any recent deploys?
 sara: pool=hosted-prod-eu-west-gpu; model=llama-3-8b-q4; last deploy ~6h ago. no infra deploys reported since. logs from gateway: `upstream returned 503: runner_exit`
 anil: can you paste the runner logs (tail -n 300)? any coredump/gcore?
 sara: paste: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] runner[pid=4321]: evicting container due to OOM
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] runtime: CUDA error: out of memory at allocLarge()
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] runtime: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f8a3b2c
[2026-03-18T09:12:14Z] stack: 0x7f8a3b2c 0x55c1b... 0x55c1f...
```
 tom: ugh. OOM -> segfault. Does ACME use large batches or many concurrent streams?
 sara: they do streaming tool-assisted responses. support note: they observed retries increasing after a client-side change to batch_size=48.
 maria: also saw a billing spike around same time, likely due to retries/timeouts. customer was using client-side exponential retry with no jitter.
 anil: this smells like dynamic batching + kv-prefetch memory ballooning. recent runtime tweak to prefetch more chunks might push memory over edge under high concurrency.
 pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD#INC-3421 (severity=sev2) — responders: eng-runtime, eng-sre
 tom: mitigations to try now: 1) global rate-limit ACME to lower concurrency 2) route to smaller model variant (llama-3-4b) 3) disable dyn-prefetch on that pool 4) restart runner nodes one-by-one to clear pinned allocations.
 sara: rolling back to 4b for that customer now. applying rate-limit via console.
 anil: repro steps we should record: 1) send 20 concurrent streaming requests with long context (~50k tokens) and batch_size=48 2) include toolcall at ~token 1024 to force kv flush 3) observe GPU memory usage climb, then OOM + segfault in runtime. Example curl to reproduce: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Model: llama-3-8b-q4" \
  -d '{"input":"<very long prompt> ...","stream":true,"batch_size":48}'
```
 tom: can you capture `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv -l 1` during repro? also enable driver-level debug logs and collect dmesg after a crash.
 sara: collecting nvidia-smi, and saved /var/log/runtime/crash-4321.log to s3://incidents/6161616262/crash-4321.log
 anil: quick patch we can try: clamp dynamic_batch to 16 on pool config and revert the prefetch increase from yesterday's runtime commit (commit b3f9a4). I'll prepare a rollback patch.
 maria: from CS side, telling customer: "We see upstream runner restarts causing 503s. We're routing you to a smaller model and throttling concurrent requests while we investigate. We'll follow up with a timeline and reproducible steps." :thumbsup:
 tom: I've paged eng-runtime lead and eng-sre. assigning followups: anil -> root-cause & runtime patch; tom -> pool restart plan & monitoring; sara -> CS updates and collect more logs.
 anil: preliminary root-cause hypothesis: prefetch buffer growth under dynbatch/concurrent streams exceeded GPU reserved slab, causing CUDA OOM, then invalid memory access during cleanup -> SIGSEGV. Need safer prefetch caps + OOM-handling guards.
 sara: next steps: 1) keep ACME on 4b until patch or capacity increase 2) monitor host-gpu OOM metric (metric: runner.gpu.oom.count) 3) run canary with patched runtime on one node.
 tom: closing note: watch p95 and 503-rate for 2 hours. will update PD and incident doc.
 maria: customer happy with fallback for now, wants ETA on patch. I'll coordinate.
 anil: I'll post the PR and link when ready.
 sara: thanks all — keeping this thread updated with logs and timeline.
